Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a short announcement for a new feature in a note-taking app: offline sync. Around 200 words.

Offline sync is now live in version 3.2.

Until now, editing a note without a connection meant your changes sat in a local queue that only flushed when you reopened the app. If you closed it on a plane, the queue stayed put. People lost work that way, and we heard about it.

The new version keeps a full local copy of your notebook on the device. You write, rename, tag, and delete against that copy, and the app records each change as a discrete operation rather than a snapshot of the file. When the connection comes back, those operations replay against the server in the order you made them. Two devices editing the same note no longer produce a "conflicted copy" for every save. They produce one merged note, with a conflict marker only where two edits touched the same paragraph within the same sync window.

Sync runs in the background, so there is no button to press. The status dot in the sidebar shows grey when the device is offline and has queued work, and clears once the queue drains.

Attachments over 25 MB still wait for a connection before they upload. We are working on chunked upload for those, but it is not in this release.

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Add a paragraph about what happens when two devices edit the same note offline.

When two devices go offline and edit the same note, neither one wins by timestamp. Each device holds its own ordered list of operations, and on reconnect the server interleaves them by the position each edit targeted rather than by the clock. Edits to different paragraphs merge without asking you anything. Edits to the same paragraph produce one note containing both versions, separated by a marker line that names the device and the local time of each edit, so you can see which draft came from the laptop on the train and which came from the phone. A delete never overrides an edit. If one device removes a note that the other was still writing in, the note stays, and the deletion is recorded as a pending action you confirm or discard from the sync panel. Nothing is dropped silently in either direction. The one case that still needs your attention is a note renamed on both devices, since a title is a single value with no paragraphs to merge. There you get a prompt listing both titles the first time you open the note after sync.

Local-first sync is now live in version 3.2.

Until now, editing a note without a connection meant your changes sat in a local queue that only flushed when you reopened the app. If you closed it on a plane, the queue stayed put. People lost work that way, and we heard about it.

The new version keeps a full local copy of your notebook on the device. That copy is the one you edit; the server holds a mirror of it. You write, rename, tag, and delete against the local copy, and the app records each change as a discrete operation rather than a snapshot of the file. When the connection comes back, those operations replay against the server in the order you made them. Two devices editing the same note no longer produce a "conflicted copy" for every save. They produce one merged note, with a conflict marker only where two edits touched the same paragraph within the same sync window.

When two devices go offline and edit the same note, neither one wins by timestamp. Each device holds its own ordered list of operations, and on reconnect the server interleaves them by the position each edit targeted rather than by the clock. Edits to different paragraphs merge without asking you anything. Edits to the same paragraph produce one note containing both versions, separated by a marker line that names the device and the local time of each edit, so you can see which draft came from the laptop on the train and which came from the phone. A delete never overrides an edit. If one device removes a note that the other was still writing in, the note stays, and the deletion is recorded as a pending action you confirm or discard from the sync panel. The one case that still needs your attention is a note renamed on both devices, since a title is a single value with no paragraphs to merge. There you get a prompt listing both titles the first time you open the note after sync.

Sync runs in the background, so there is no button to press. The status dot in the sidebar shows grey when the device is offline and has queued work, and clears once the queue drains.

Attachments over 25 MB still wait for a connection before they upload. We are working on chunked upload for those, but it is not in this release.
